extracted.intended_audience: ERC peer reviewers (Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators, Remote Referees) for Starting and Consolidator Grant calls
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing individual and panel-based peer review of ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant proposals under the Horizon Europe Work Programme; covers two-step evaluation, scoring, conflicts of interest, review content and format, and panel deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence as sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of proposals is panel-based, peer review evaluation with excellence as the sole criterion; applied to the ground-breaking nature and ambition of the Research Project and to the intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessments must be made against the evaluation criterion and its detailed elements alone. Incorrect application or use of irrelevant criteria is a procedural error and may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Step 1 evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 1: To what extent does the research address important scientific questions? To what extent are the project’s objectives ambitious and will it advance the frontier of knowledge?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part I (Part B1) should present envisaged research, current state of knowledge, scientific question, objectives, and overall approach; all essential information must be covered in this section because it forms the basis for Step 1 decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Step 2 evaluation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2: To what extent does the research address important scientific questions? To what extent are the project’s objectives ambitious and will it advance the frontier of knowledge? To what extent are the research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project? To what extent are the timescales and resources adequate and properly justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2 reviewers assess the full proposal (Parts B1 and B2) including detailed methodology, work plan, risk assessment and mitigation, and justification for requested budget and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator evaluation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 1 and Step 2: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct groundbreaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative and original thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess intellectual capacity and creativity; consider transition to independence, diverse career paths, noteworthy community contributions, and possible career breaks or major life events when judging the track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal numerical mark scale (Research Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal marks are awarded using a numerical scale: 5 (Outstanding), 4 (Excellent), 3 (Very Good), 2 (Good), 1 (Non-competitive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks may be given in integers or halves; use of the full range of marks is recommended. The proposal numerical mark should be consistent with the explanatory comments. Proposal marks are not directly communicated to applicants (panel scores are).

rubrics_metrics.name: PI overall qualitative assessment categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall qualitative assessment for the Principal Investigator with five options: Outstanding / Excellent / Very Good / Good / Non-competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees provide a three-option funding recommendation only: highly recommended, recommended, or not recommended. PI qualitative assessment should be consistent with comments and may be optionally provided by reviewers at Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel final scoring categories and definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1 panel scores: A invited (excellent and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2), A not invited (excellent but not ranked high enough), B (high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2), C (not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2). Step 2 scores: A (fully meets the ERC's excellence criterion and recommended for funding if funds available), B (meets some but not all aspects and not recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A maximum of 44 proposals per panel can be passed to Step 2; Step 1 Bs receive ranking ranges; Step 1 C proposals receive a standard panel comment and individual reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part I (B1) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I should present the envisaged research, lay out the current state of knowledge, explain the scientific question and the objectives of the project, and present the overall approach or research strategy to reach the goals of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Part I forms the basis for the panel's Step 1 decision, all essential information must be included in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part II (B2) content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II should be a detailed explanation of project implementation, including research methodology, work plan, risk assessment and mitigating measures, justification for the requested budget and resources, and any further necessary background not included in Part I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II is reviewed at Step 2 together with detailed budget table and resource descriptions extracted from administrative Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual reviewers' comments — quality standards (Do's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviews should be good quality, genuine, substantial, and polite; provide explanatory comments for the Research Project and a qualitative assessment for the PI; use dispassionate, analytical, and unambiguous language; use grammatically correct, complete, clear sentences with no jargon; ensure critical comments are constructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments form part of the Evaluation Report sent to applicants and must therefore be carefully formulated. Ensure comments are in line with marks/funding recommendation and avoid referring to marks in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual reviewers' comments — prohibited content and Don'ts
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid comments that merely describe or summarise the proposal, avoid self-declaration of insufficient expertise, avoid dismissive statements about applicant/proposed science/field, avoid reference to applicant’s age, nationality, gender, personal matters, or Host Institution, avoid direct comparisons with other proposals or previous assessments, avoid copy-paste from the proposal or other reviewers, avoid comments on ethical and security aspects (these are handled after scientific evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing achievements, focus on scientific content and refrain from surrogate measures such as Journal Impact Factors. Societal impact is not an ERC evaluation criterion. Be aware of and try to mitigate unconscious bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest rules and list
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts must confirm absence of conflicts of interest; a list of conflicts is displayed in the online system (examples include: being PI or team member in the proposal; involvement in preparation; benefit from acceptance/rejection; employment/contract with entities involved in past 3 years; director/trustee/partner in entity involved; scientific collaboration in past 5 years; mentor/mentee relationship; family or close personal ties; scientific rivalry/hostility; being National Contact Point or EEN worker; member of an EU programme committee; any other situation precluding impartial review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must declare conflicts when accepting to review and when submitting their individual review. Panel Chairs avoid assigning proposals to reviewers with declared conflicts. A breach may lead to termination of contract/appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and contact rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers shall not engage in any contact with applicants or beneficiaries about the evaluation, neither during nor after the evaluation; during individual remote review there shall be no discussions of proposals between reviewers and Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing the Expert Contract or Letter of Appointment reviewers accept confidentiality conditions and data use rules. Suspected procedural errors or inappropriate comments in reviews should be reported to the Panel Chair and ERCEA Scientific Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of roles and reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators (PEVs), and Remote Referees have defined roles: Panel Members act as generalists, may be Lead Reviewers, write individual reviews, attend meetings; Panel Chairs chair meetings, allocate proposals and remote referees, ensure deliverables quality; PEVs assist remote evaluation and act as specialists when selected; Remote Referees provide specialised assessments (2–5 per proposal, typically non-paid) and do not attend panel meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Reviewers introduce proposals at panel meetings and draft panel comments (except for proposals scored C). Panel Members are expected to be available for both panel meetings; Panel Chairs select and approve Remote Referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of reviewers per proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal shall be reviewed by at least three peer reviewers as required by the ERC Rules of submission and evaluation under Horizon Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees (specialists) are typically 2–5 per proposal at Step 2; Panel Evaluators may be used to supplement reviews where expertise is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget assessment and recommendations (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2 the panel analyses the budget, its justification and the requested contribution; recommendations on reduction may be made if some expenses (excluding salary costs) are not considered fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget cuts must be documented and explained in the panel comment based on analysis of resources necessary to carry out the work. Across-the-board cuts are not allowed. Avoid recommending on salaries (they depend on national/institutional rules). Avoid resource recommendations at Step 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and eligibility checks and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility and eligibility of submitted proposals are assessed by the ERCEA; reviewers who consider a proposal potentially inadmissible or ineligible should report it immediately to ERCEA Scientific Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some checks (e.g., date of successful PhD defence, eligibility extension requests) are run after Step 1; proposals may be declared inadmissible/ineligible during or after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multi- and inter-disciplinary proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter- and multi-disciplinary proposals are encouraged; the applicant's initial panel choice is paramount; proposals may be flagged as interdisciplinary and the panel may request additional reviews from other panels; applicants may indicate a second panel if cross-panel/domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary panels are multidisciplinary and are responsible to ensure cross-panel/cross-domain proposals receive equal and fair treatment. Panels may reallocate proposals between panels by agreement of the two Panel Chairs when necessary for expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel ranking procedure, voting and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking is the outcome of panel discussion excluding members with conflicts of interest. Consensus is preferred, but panels may use voting systems (majority vote) or cumulative ranking systems to expedite ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Panel Member has one vote per proposal under consideration. Panel Members with a conflict cannot discuss, vote for, or rank that proposal. Step 1 Bs and Cs have specific ranking/reporting rules (e.g., Step 1 Bs are ranked with 10% intervals within B category).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comment content and separation of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel comments reflect the main points of panel discussion and must clearly explain the reason(s), respecting the ERC evaluation criterion, which make(s) the proposal succeed or fail. Panels must ensure scientific feedback is clearly distinct from budget recommendations to the ERCEA (which are binding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Reviewers draft panel comments for A not invited and B in Step 1 and for all proposals at Step 2; panel approves final version. Standard panel comments are used for Step 1 C proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers' practical conduct & meeting efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Members should familiarise themselves with all proposals in the panel, assess a subset in detail, and prepare for interviews by identifying strengths, weaknesses and concerns raised in individual reviews. Preparatory remote work is required to ensure highly efficient panel meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members must deliver concise but substantial reviews, be fully available for panel meetings (usually on-site), and prepare for Step 2 interviews (panel decides interview format).
